title: Universal Defect Statistics in Reverse Quenches
authors: Eduard J. Braun, Daniel Rubin, Margaux Cartier, Gerhard Zürn, Matthias Weidemüller
abstract: We derive an extension of the generalized Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM), which provides a stochastic approach to defect formation, to reverse quench protocols. While the universal scaling behavior of defects in reverse quenches has been observed previously in certain 1D chains, we argument from a probability-theoretical perspective that this scaling persists in general, and is given by the double of the defect density variance in forward quenches. We validate these results analytically for the one-dimensional transverse field Ising model and numerically for its bond-disordered variant governed by an infinite randomness fixed point. Starting from the paramagnetic phase, this protocol relies solely on global control of the system's magnetic field and global magnetization measurements, enabling the extraction of critical exponents without microscopic access to individual defects. This approach offers a robust and experimentally feasible method for probing quantum critical behavior through entirely global operations.
summary: This paper extends the Kibble-Zurek mechanism to predict defect formation statistics during reverse quench protocols in quantum systems. It establishes a quantitative relationship showing that the defect variance in reverse quenches is twice the variance found in forward quenches. The theory is rigorously tested using the 1D transverse field Ising model, offering a powerful tool for characterizing quantum critical dynamics globally.
main_problem: The paper derives an extension of the Kibble-Zurek mechanism (gKZM) to analyze defect formation statistics during non-equilibrium quench protocols, specifically focusing on reverse quenches.
main_result: The universal scaling behavior of defects in reverse quenches is shown to be related to, and given by, double the defect density variance observed in forward quenches.
method: The analysis uses a probability-theoretical approach based on the gKZM, validating results analytically for the 1D transverse field Ising model and numerically for its bond-disordered variant.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum spin systems, exemplified by the one-dimensional transverse field Ising model (TFIM) undergoing controlled quenches across a critical point.
key_observables: Defect density ($n_{def}$), defect density variance ($	ext{Var}(n_{def})$), and magnetization ($\langle \hat{S}_x angle$).
important_parameters: Quench time ($	au_Q$), critical exponents ($\mu$), and the system size ($L$ or $N$).
main_assumptions: The approach assumes the validity of the gKZM framework and relies on global control and measurement of the system's magnetic field and magnetization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the adiabatic–impulse approximation and the specific protocol for a reverse quench in an Ising ferromagnet, showing domain wall evolution.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the gKZM and its application to forward quenches, establishing scaling laws for defect density and variance. It then extends this theory to reverse quench protocols, deriving the key relationship between forward and reverse quench statistics. Finally, it validates these theoretical results using the TFIM model, both in its clean and bond-disordered forms.
why_interesting: The methodology provides a robust, experimentally feasible way to probe quantum critical behavior using only global measurements, which is highly relevant for experimental quantum simulation platforms.
